title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this part of 'Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques)' Grothendieck axiomatizes 1-dimensional topological 'forms', meaning curves and 1-manifolds, without using point-set topology. A model of 1-form is a triple 𝔛 = (𝓛, S, ∂). Here 𝓛 is a set of points, S ⊂ 𝔓(𝓛) is a family of 'segments', and ∂ : S → 𝔓₂(𝓛) assigns to each segment its two endpoints.

The previous page showed that a 1-segment structure on a set L with ∂L = {x₀, x₁} is the same as a 'bi-order'. This is a pair of mutually opposite total orders such that:
- there are distinct least and greatest elements (Card L > 1);
- the order is divisible (dense);
- it is locally filtrant and cofiltrant.
Swapping x₀ and x₁ replaces the order by its opposite, and the axioms are self-dual.

This page begins with a definition: an orientation of a segment is the choice of one of its endpoints, or equivalently of one of the two opposite orders making up the bi-order.

It then turns to regular models, those with 𝓛 = 𝓛_r (presumably every point is a 'regular', i.e. interior manifold-like, point). Grothendieck defines a reflexive, symmetric relation on 𝓛: x and y are related if some I ∈ S contains both in its (decorated) closure. For regular models, by Cor. 2 to F4, this is equivalent to x, y lying in the interior Ī° of the closure of some segment. He takes the generated equivalence relation; its classes form π₀(𝔛), the connected components. He then notes there is an evident notion of sum (disjoint/direct sum) of models of 1-forms, and that every 1-form is the sum of its connected components.

The next page reduces the study of regular models to connected regular ones. For a connected regular model it constructs a canonical 2-element set ω, the orientation torsor. ω comes with a transitive system of isomorphisms to each ∂I (I ∈ S) and to each B_x, the set of two 'branches' or local orientations at x. This is the combinatorial analogue of the fact that a connected 1-manifold has exactly two orientations, i.e. its orientation double cover is trivial.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The definition of π₀ via the equivalence relation generated by 'lying in a common (interior of a closed) segment' is standard and correct.
The equivalence of the two relations depends on Cor. 2 to F4 and on the regularity hypothesis, neither of which can be checked from this page.

ideas.what: Orientation of a segment as the choice of an endpoint, equivalently of one of the two opposite orders of its bi-order
ideas.modern_name: orientation of an interval / Z/2-torsor of orientations

ideas.what: π₀ of a combinatorial model of 1-form, as classes of the equivalence relation generated by 'x, y in a common segment'
Decomposition of a 1-form as the disjoint sum of its connected components
Order-theoretic and incidence axiomatization of 1-dimensional topological forms via segments with boundary (program of a 'géométrie des formes')
ideas.modern_name: synthetic/combinatorial models of 1-manifolds and graphs; tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: various; Grothendieck's call for 'tame topology' is in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches the tame-topology motivation, not this axiomatics

missed.claim: This page belongs to an unpublished axiomatic program defining 1-dimensional topological forms purely by (𝓛, S, ∂) with order-theoretic axioms, independently of point-set topology. The content of this page itself (π₀, orientations) is routine; the program as a whole was never developed or published.
missed.quote: Considérons la relation d'équivalence engendrée. L'ens. des classes d'équivalence est noté π₀(𝔛)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal and tame topology and with combinatorial models of curves, but this page adds nothing technically new.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds routine definitions (orientation of a segment, connected components, sum decomposition) inside Grothendieck's little-known axiomatic 'geometry of forms'. The interest lies in the program, not in this page's content.
transcription_corrections: 'Considérons la relation sur 𝓛, en x,y' probably reads 'Considérons la relation sur 𝓛, entre x, y'.
'[ou, en vertu du cor. 2 à F4), si 𝓛 = 𝓛_r, et (réguliers ...) à' probably reads 'équivalente, en vertu du cor. 2 à F4) (si 𝓛 = 𝓛_r, i.e. ...), à'.

'notion évidente de morphismes directs des modèles' probably reads 'notion évidente de somme(s) directe(s) (disjointe) de modèles'. This fits the continuation 'toute 1-forme s'identifie [à la somme de] ses comp. connexes'.
'et on voit que les 1-formes s'identifie' probably reads 'et on voit que toute 1-forme s'identifie'.
'Cette relation' is written 'Cette relation est réflexive et symétrique' (confirmed).
